To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the growth of the date palm was significantly affected by heavy metals contamination in the soil, (2) the growth of maize was not significantly affected by heavy metal contamination in the soil (3) the growth of alfalfa was significantly affected by the contamination of the soil with heavy metals, and (4) the growth of sunflower was significantly affected by contamination of the soil by heavy metals.
the inter cropping of date palm with corn is a promising strategy for improving plant growth and phytoextraction of heavy metals in polluted soils.
the intercropping date palm and corn in a heavy metal polluted soil, the date palm and corn showed a higher uptake of heavy metals than the sole crop of date palm and corn, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth and heavy metals uptake by date palm and other plants in monoculture and dual culture in heavy metal contaminated soil.
the effect of intercropping date palm with maize on the growth of date palm and heavy metals uptake by both plants.
the use of date palm intercrops for phytoextraction of heavy metals from polluted soil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of date palm as a phytoremediator in mono culture and inter cropping systems with other plant species would be a good option in the remediation of heavy metals in agricultural soil.
intercropping of date palm with corn was the most suitable for growth and heavy metals uptake in the polluted agricultural soil.
the inter cropping technique did not significantly affect growth and heavy metal uptake of the tested crops.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
date palm inter cropped with corn recorded the highest fresh and dry weights and corn intercropped with date palm recorded the highest uptake index of heavy metals.
intercropping date palm and corn was the best treatment for the removal of heavy metals.
date palm can be used as a phytoremediation plant for the heavy metals contaminated soil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intercropping with date palm can be used to increase biomass and heavy metals uptake from contaminated soil and can be used as a remediation strategy.
date palm is a suitable plant species for the phytoremediation of heavy metal contaminated agricultural soils.
the intercropping of date palm with sunflower and corn can improve the growth of the date palm and the accumulation of heavy metals in polluted soils.
